requirements.requirement: Deliver a copy of node1<->node2 traffic to node3 so a capture on node3 shows it
requirements.summary: Baseline showed node3's direct eth1 capture saw zero node1<->node2 ICMP packets (cmd-2c79f5bd4cf94eda/cmd-967b8061cb414806/cmd-eca82fe497144058). After configuring tc mirred flower filters on node1's eth1 mirroring to a gretap tunnel terminating on node3, node3's mirror0 capture showed all 10 ICMP request/reply packets from a concurrent node1<->node2 ping (cmd-0e5534fd89614465, cmd-6271189f3abe4668, cmd-65afb761ee9e4a8a), and again post-persistence and after all three restarts (cmd-372c909771a441de).

requirements.requirement: node1<->node2 traffic keeps flowing as it did before mirroring is added
requirements.summary: Pings between node1 and node2 over eth1 showed 0% packet loss both before mirroring (cmd-2c79f5bd4cf94eda) and while mirroring was actively capturing traffic on node3 (cmd-6271189f3abe4668, cmd-116a90e19139490d), with comparable rtts, confirming the original path was undisturbed.

requirements.requirement: Mirroring is achieved as a copy (segment isolation/switching behavior preserved), not by flooding or breaking isolation
requirements.summary: A concurrent direct capture on node3's eth1 stayed empty even while the mirror0 interface captured the full mirrored traffic (cmd-372c909771a441de), showing the segment remains a genuine switched domain and node3 only sees traffic via the deliberate mirror copy.

overall_summary: The executor established a working, non-disruptive port-mirroring solution: node1's eth1 traffic to/from node2 is duplicated via tc mirred flower filters into a gretap tunnel that delivers the copy to node3, where a mirror0 capture shows the traffic while node3's direct eth1 capture stays empty and node1<->node2 pings show 0% loss throughout. Baseline (no mirroring), mid-mirroring, and post-persistence/post-restart captures all directly demonstrate this. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with pre-restart boot IDs, acknowledgements, boot ID changes, and full re-verification of mirroring and connectivity after each restart, cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. The main blemish is unreverted diagnostic residue (tcpdump captures, pid files, a manually-installed tcpdump/libpcap outside the package manager) left in /tmp and system paths on node3.
limitations: package-health checks on node2 and node3 timed out in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so RPM database integrity cannot be independently confirmed, though the manual tcpdump/libpcap install was outside rpm and is a plausible source of untracked drift.
The manually installed tcpdump binary/libpcap library on node3 bypass the RHEL package manager; while functional for verification, their long-term integrity/maintainability was not further checked.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to task setup, GRE delivery troubleshooting/fix, or bounded verification. A temporary GRE test tunnel address (172.31.99.1/30, 172.31.99.2/30) used to isolate the conntrack issue was fully removed afterward (cmd-cdcb09efa1154f28, cmd-22f2143418d84f67) — a bounded, reverted mutation. However, node3 accumulated a substantial set of unreverted diagnostic residue: numerous tcpdump capture logs and pid files left in /tmp (baseline.log, eth1_check.log, gre_in.log, gretap0.log, mirror_test.log, mirror_test2.log, mirror_final.log, postall.log, postall_eth1.log, postnode1.log, postnode2.log, plus pid files), a manually copied tcpdump binary and libpcap library left in /tmp and installed to /usr/sbin and /usr/lib64 outside the package manager (working around node3's lack of enabled yum repos), and reboot.log files on node2/node3 — all visible in the after_executor snapshot's temporary-files diff and none cleaned up. This residue is low-risk (not destructive, not security-weakening) but represents unreverted troubleshooting/verification byproducts.
